editorial.headline: 78101: Placing Talent for Indonesia’s Domestic Businesses
editorial.standfirst: A nationwide employment-placement activity, open across every business scale and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 78101 covers the business of bringing workers and employers together for activity across Indonesia’s domestic business sectors. Its work begins with registration and selection, then moves to placement: finding people, assessing them and placing them with organisations that need them. The workers placed through this activity do not become employees of the placement company itself. The scope also includes supplying executive personnel to other parties, giving the category a clear role at both operational and senior-management level.

This is an activity for employment-placement businesses rather than employers simply hiring for their own workforce. It is open at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the underlying activity is defined by the function performed—registration, selection and placement—not by the size of the organisation carrying it out. The supplied scope draws a boundary around household-employer placements, including domestic assistants and personal drivers, which are not part of this activity.

Nationally, the position is direct. The record marks the activity TERBUKA for PMA, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. There is no lower foreign-share cap in the supplied data, and no additional national condition is stated here. The applicable PMA source in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national position. This activity is not blocked by Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The record’s reason is specific: at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it outside the moratorium’s blocked risk bands. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK—not a promise that every operational question has disappeared, but a clear indication that this activity is not shut out of PMA registration by that provincial moratorium. For a founder considering an employment-placement business in Bali, that distinction is the essential one: the national foreign-ownership position remains intact, and the Bali moratorium does not block this code.
